en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Pāricchattaka Tree within the Itthivimāna (The Female Vimānas)
3. The Mansion of the Couch "On a most excellent couch, variegated with jewels and gold,
a sublime bed strewn with flowers;
There you dwell, O goddess of great majesty,
manifesting various and manifold supernatural powers;
and these nymphs surround you on every side.
They dance, sing, and rejoice;
you have attained the sovereignty of the gods, O lady of great power.
What merit did you perform while you were a human being?
“By what means have you come to possess such blazing majesty,
and why does your radiance illuminate all directions?
“I was born among humans as a human being.”
I was a daughter-in-law in a wealthy family;
free from anger, I followed the will of my husband,
and I was diligent in observing the Uposatha.
Having become a human being, young and free from evil,
with a confident heart I delighted my husband;
day and night I was pleasant in my conduct.
In the past, I was possessed of virtue.
I abstained from taking life and refrained from theft;
my body was completely purified, and I lived a pure life of celibacy.
I did not drink intoxicants, nor did I speak falsehood;
I was one who fulfilled the training rules.
On the fourteenth and the fifteenth, [I observed the uposatha].
And on the eighth day of the fortnight,
as well as during the fortnight of miracles,
I was one whose mind was full of serene faith.
Endowed with the eight factors and practicing in accordance with the Dhamma,
I observed the Uposatha with a joyful heart;
and this noble [Uposatha] endowed with the excellent eight factors—
Having undertaken wholesome deeds that bring about happiness,
I was formerly a disciple of the Sugata, a virtuous woman living in accordance with her husband.
Having performed such wholesome karma in the world of the living, she partakes in excellence;
with the breakup of the body, in the life hereafter—
Having attained divine power, they have come to a happy destination;
surrounded by throngs of celestial nymphs, they dwell in delightful and excellent palaces and mansions.
"The self-luminous hosts of gods delight me,
who have come to this celestial mansion of long life.
Thus ends the third chapter, the Pallaṅka-vimāna.
